title: Closed herringbone stitch
subtitle: Touching herringbone rows that create a solid fill and the basis of shadow work
excerpt: Closed herringbone stitch removes the backward step of ordinary herringbone so that each stitch meets the previous one exactly at the guide lines. Worked on the back of sheer fabric it becomes shadow work, casting a soft shadow through to the right side.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), herringbone entry.

content.text: Closed herringbone stitch is worked like herringbone stitch but with no space between stitches: each diagonal starts exactly where the previous one ended at the guide line. On the right side of the fabric this makes a solid zigzag band. Worked on the wrong side of organdie or silk organza, with the stitches touching on the back, it becomes shadow work. The crossing threads show through the sheer fabric as a soft, filled shape on the right side.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 1 to 2 strands; for shadow work use a single strand in a colour that reads well through sheer cloth

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Cotton or linen for surface work; silk organza or organdie for shadow work

content.text: Transfer the shape outline as two parallel lines (or the two edges of a leaf or petal shape). For shadow work, transfer to the wrong side of the fabric.
Bring the needle up at A on the bottom line. Insert at B on the top line, directly above and slightly to the right. Bring the needle up at C on the top line, exactly at A's level but touching B.
Insert at D on the bottom line, touching A. Bring up at E on the bottom line, touching D. No gap is left: each new stitch begins at the end point of the previous one.
Continue to the end of the shape. The back of the fabric will show two parallel rows of back stitches running along each guide line. On the right side, the crossing threads form a solid zigzag fill.
For shadow work, turn to the right side to check the shape is filling evenly. Adjust tension: too tight pulls the sheer fabric into a ridge.

items.symptom: Gaps appear between stitches on the surface
items.cause: Each stitch did not begin exactly at the end of the previous one.
items.fix: Place the needle into the same hole as the last stitch exit to close the gap. A magnifier helps on fine fabrics.

items.symptom: The sheer fabric puckers on shadow work
items.cause: Thread tension is too high, pulling the fabric.
items.fix: Use a single strand and pull each stitch through gently. Keep the hoop drum-tight before stitching.

items.symptom: The shape on the right side looks uneven
items.cause: Stitches on the back vary in length, so the shadow coverage is patchy.
items.fix: Mark equal-interval dots along both guide lines on the wrong side before starting.
